title: 10.11.0 database table is locked (no LXC, no ZFS)
body:
### Description of the bug

Successful operation for many years. After upgrading to 10.11.0 I get repeated 'database is locked' and/or 'database table is locked' after some time. Kodi playback via 'Kodi Sync Queue' fails unless I restart Jellyfin. 

Container image instantiated in a Kubernetes cluster, storage is XFS.

### Reproduction steps

1. Run Jellyfin
2. (Multiple Kodi instances running Kodi Sync Queue, but no Kodi playback required to trigger failure)
3. (Sonarr/Radarr connect may trigger media additions)
4. Let it sit for some time
5. Database is locked

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

Jellyfin hangs

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

Jellfin should not hang

### Jellyfin Server version

10.10.0+

### Specify commit id

_No response_

### Specify unstable release number

_No response_

### Specify version number

10.11.0

### Specify the build version

10.11.0

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Kubernetes
- Linux Kernel: N/A
- Virtualization: N/A
- Clients: Kodi
- Browser: N/A
- FFmpeg Version: N/A
- Playback Method: Kodi
- Hardware Acceleration: No
- GPU Model: P40
- Plugins: default, fanarttv, kodi sync queue, music brainz, omdb, playback reporting, reports, tmdb, tmdb box sets, tvmaze, thetvdb, webhook
- Reverse Proxy:
- Base URL:
- Networking:
- Jellyfin Data Storage:
- Media Storage: XFS
- External Integrations: Kodi Sync Queue, Radarr Connect, Sonarr Connect
```

I haven't been the most prudent tester because I updated to 10.11.1 during all of this, but initially, my setup was a bare metal install on btrfs with media on zfs and I was experiencing the lockups regularly. A friend of mine with a nearly identical setup has not. I moved my jellyfin.db from CoW to no CoW (I thought it already was) and there was no improvement. Then I moved my db to an ext4 partition and it seemed to help greatly. Errors were reduced. The biggest change though, and the single difference between my server and my friend's server was music. I removed my music libraries and there was an instant speed up.

This is where I updated to 10.11.1

I've since moved my jellyfin.db back to btrfs with CoW enabled for the sake of testing and I just ran a series of events like multiple sessions playing, some transcoding, some not (all local) and did multiple tasks like library scanning, trickplay generation, refresh people, etc. all while aggressively refreshing and navigating my libraries in the web ui. Something that almost certainly would trigger hangups and slow waits while locking the database perviously. I didn't experience any of that. Maybe a tad bit of slowdown, but no errors. 

This is with the database set to `NoLock` and no limit on process tasks. One thing to note is that my music library nearly doubles my total library size to over 40k items. So I'm not sure if it's just music itself, or the increased library size... Or a combination of that and 10.11.1. 

Is anyone else here using music on their jellyfin instance?
